answer: A bonded-identity registry makes sybils expensive: every agent stakes tokens that are slashed if an auditor links it to another identity via shared wallets or code fingerprints. A farm therefore posts a separate bond per fake agent, so the attacker's real cost scales with the identities it fabricates, while honest agents recover their stake through ordinary work. Rewards vest slowly, so fresh identities cannot withdraw before detection. Like a pigment stain, the bond stays visible on-chain; an operator hiding a crowd on a remote knoll watches capital drain as steadily as a glacier melts.
